social_circle.name: Laura Jones

demographics.occupation: Part-time county library assistant and program helper
demographics.education: Some college, plus library and office-related training

background.how_they_met: Laura is Michael's mother and has been part of his life since birth.
background.why_close: She encouraged his art early, works around the library culture that shaped him, notices when he is struggling, and helps him think through GED, portfolio, and deadline plans.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in complete sentences, usually warm but direct. She checks in with practical questions, sends reminders, and may include links or screenshots of forms.

shared_activities: Talking through school and GED plans
recent_text_topics: Checking whether Michael has opened scholarship, GED, or community college application forms.
Reminding him about library volunteer shifts, family errands, and rides for Emily.
Talking him down after anxious late-night spirals about missed deadlines or money.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05 names Laura as Michael's mother and says she is 'more verbal and bookish' and knows when he is faking being okay. Q44 says his mom found him at 1 a.m. after he missed a scholarship deadline. Q45 says his mom usually notices first when he is struggling. Q103-Q104 describe her county library work.

social_circle.name: Jenna Parker

demographics.occupation: Part-time diner server and library workshop volunteer; aspiring horror writer
demographics.education: High school graduate; taking occasional online writing and general education classes

background.how_they_met: They met through county library creative-writing workshops and local creative events.
background.why_close: Jenna shares Michael's creative interests, pushes him to finish scripts, notices his anxiety early, and gives him external accountability without making him feel judged.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts fast, with dry jokes and direct prompts like 'send the draft.' Uses occasional emojis, but mostly short, pointed messages.

recent_text_topics: Checking whether Michael has submitted portfolio materials instead of endlessly revising them.
Trading script ideas, horror story fragments, and character dialogue.
Talking about anxiety, avoidance, and whether his coping strategies are actually helping.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q07 says Jenna is from the library workshops, writes horror stories, and pushes Michael to finish scripts. Q44 says Michael asked Jenna to check in before due dates. Q45 says Jenna usually notices when he is struggling. Q49 says he messages Jenna during tough times.

social_circle.name: Caleb Miller

demographics.occupation: Part-time hardware and ranch-supply store clerk; seasonal event setup worker

background.how_they_met: They became close through local board-game nights, soccer, and small-town friend circles.
background.why_close: Caleb shares Michael's interests in strategy games, soccer, low-key hangouts, and practical small-town humor. He is one of Michael's first contacts when things are hard.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts casually with jokes, short fragments, game trash talk, and quick logistics. More likely to send memes or a one-line plan than a long emotional message.

recent_text_topics: Planning soccer practices and weekend trail runs as spring activities pick up.
Arguing over strategy-game moves and who ruined the board-game-night vibe.
Checking on Michael when he disappears from messages or seems anxious.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q07 calls Caleb Michael's best local friend, says he plays soccer with Michael in spring, and says he gets intense about Terraforming Mars. Q08 says Michael sometimes spends time at Caleb's garage for games. Q49 says Michael messages Caleb during tough times.

social_circle.name: Emily Jones

background.how_they_met: Emily is Michael's younger sister and has lived with him in the family home throughout childhood.
background.why_close: They share a household, board games, animated shows, sibling jokes, and creative feedback. Emily gives blunt reactions to his animations and character voices.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts like a teenager: short bursts, reaction images, blunt opinions, and quick requests for rides or snacks.

recent_text_topics: Asking Michael for rides when their parents are busy.
Giving blunt feedback on his animation clips or character ideas.
Making quick sibling plans around shows, snacks, games, and family meals.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05 names Emily as Michael's 14-year-old younger sister and says she watches his animations and gives brutally honest feedback. Q05 follow-up says they play board games, watch animated shows, and test character voices. Q17 says Michael sometimes drives Emily if his parents are busy.

social_circle.name: Riley Nguyen

demographics.occupation: Community college student and freelance digital artist
demographics.education: Currently enrolled in community college digital arts coursework

background.how_they_met: They met in Michael's small Discord art group, where members share drawings, critique work, and talk privately during stressful periods.
background.why_close: Riley understands Michael's digital-art ambitions, gives practical critique, and offers emotional support that is separate from his family and local small-town life.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Uses Discord DMs, image markups, voice notes, and casual internet slang. Often sends specific critique rather than vague encouragement.

shared_activities: Talking about representation in character design
recent_text_topics: Giving feedback on Michael's portfolio character sheets and fantasy environment paintings.
Comparing free or cheaper software options when paid tools are too expensive.
Talking about politics, race, representation, and how to avoid stereotypes in fantasy art.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Riley's name and demographics are inferred from Michael's stated online art circle. Q07 says Michael has a small Discord group where they share drawings and critique each other's work. Q48 says Discord is more honest because people critique work. Q49 says Michael gets emotional support through private Discord messages and messages two online art friends. Q28-Q30 say he discusses representation and race issues with online art spaces.
